key_insight: Routers can be trained without human labels by using LLMs to generate synthetic queries and answers from high-level task descriptions, enabling reliable skill estimation and expert selection in annotation-free settings.
problem_solved: How to train model routers when ground-truth labeled data is unavailable or user request distributions are heterogeneous and unknown, avoiding costly human annotation.
method: Use generator LLMs to produce diverse synthetic query–answer pairs from high-level task descriptions, creating an annotation-free training corpus.
Train a router to estimate each candidate expert model's skill/performance on the generated data (skill estimation), then learn a mapping from inputs to the best expert.
At inference, use the learned router to select the optimal expert per query, improving task-specific performance without labeled ground-truth.
impact: Enables deployment of dynamic, annotation-free routing systems that reduce labeling costs and adapt to varied user requests, making model selection scalable and practical for real-world AI services.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Task descriptions → Generator LLM → Synthetic dataset → Router training → Inference routing to expert models
Comparison bar chart: Router trained on generated data vs. labeled-data baseline vs. naive routing (e.g., single best model)
Heatmap or matrix: Estimated skill scores of multiple experts across diverse synthetic tasks
Icon set: generator LLM (pen/robot), router (switchboard), expert models (multiple servers), and no-annotation badge
paper_title: Routing with Generated Data: Annotation-Free LLM Skill Estimation and Expert Selection
paper_authors: Tianyi Niu, Justin Chih-Yao Chen, Genta Indra Winata, Shi-Xiong Zhang, Supriyo Chakraborty
